title: Chocolate Crinkle Cookies
subtitle: fudgy, brownie-like chocolate cookies rolled in icing sugar so they crack open like snow on bark
imageAlt: Dark chocolate cookies with white icing-sugar crackled tops piled on a white plate on a navy napkin
servingsNote: about 24 cookies: 2 each, and a tin to share

beforeYouStart.text: The dough is soft like brownie batter and needs at least 1 hour in the fridge (included) before you can roll it. It keeps up to 2 days.
Use plain unsweetened cocoa powder, not hot chocolate mix.

steps.title: Wet mix
steps.text: Whisk the cocoa, sugar and oil in a large bowl until smooth. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

steps.title: Add the dry
steps.text: Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in another bowl, then stir into the chocolate mixture just until no flour shows.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, until firm enough to scoop.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line 2 baking sheets with parchment. Put the icing sugar in a shallow bowl. Scoop the dough by the tablespoon, roll into balls and roll each thickly in the icing sugar. Set them 5 cm apart.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake one sheet at a time 10–11 minutes, until the edges are set and the tops are cracked; the centres should still look soft. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then move to a rack.

fixIt.fix: Chill longer, and roll with lightly oiled hands.
The icing sugar melted in. Roll the balls thickly, or roll them in granulated sugar first, then icing sugar.
The dough warmed up. Keep the bowl in the fridge between sheets.
Overbaked. Pull them while the centres still look soft; they set as they cool.

saleTip: Cocoa powder is often cheaper in the No Frills bulk aisle; buy what you need for one batch.
swap: Melted butter instead of oil: same amount. A little richer, slightly less fudgy.
leftovers: Crumble over vanilla ice cream, or sandwich two with a spoon of icing.
doneness: Edges set, tops cracked, centres still soft. Don't taste the raw dough: it has raw egg and raw flour.
source: Based on tested chocolate crinkle methods (Betty Crocker, Canadian Living): a cocoa-and-oil dough chilled firm, rolled in icing sugar, baked at 180°C (350°F).
prepAhead: Keep the dough covered in the fridge up to 2 days.
Freeze baked cookies up to 3 months; roll in a little fresh icing sugar after thawing.
reheat: Not needed. Serve at room temperature.

fancy.note: Chopped dark chocolate folded in for melty pockets, and a hint of orange.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: whisk in the orange zest with the vanilla.
stepNotes.1: Fancy: fold in the chopped chocolate last.

plating: Stack them on a dark plate so the white cracks pop.
Dust with a little extra icing sugar just before serving.

why.0-2: Oil keeps the cookies fudgy and soft for days, even after chilling.
why.1-0: A thick icing-sugar coat stays white while the cookie spreads and cracks underneath it.

funFact: Crinkle cookies were a mid-century North American church-cookbook favourite; Betty Crocker's version from the 1950s made them a Christmas staple.

keeps.note: roll in a little fresh icing sugar after thawing
keeps.thaw: On the counter in their container, about 1 hour
